ASP.NET Core DI supports transient, scoped, and singleton lifetimes. Scoped commonly means one request; injecting a scoped service into a singleton creates invalid lifetime ownership.

In a production system, use constructor injection, keep singletons thread-safe, avoid service-location, and create explicit scopes only for owned background work. At senior depth, I would quantify the relevant latency, scale, correctness, security, and cost limits, compare the simplest credible alternative, and name the measured threshold that would change the design.
